name: Flavio
author: marketgoo

sections.description:
Flavio is the Online Visibility Agent for small businesses. It scans your site, then automatically fixes what it can & asks for your input only when it truly needs it, so you get your time back instead of yet another technical checklist.

If you want your site to be easier to find, easier to understand, and better prepared for how people search today across Google, local results, and AI assistants, then Flavio is for you. No expertise required! Flavio acts, you just watch your visibility improve.

What Flavio helps with

Flavio focuses on the areas that matter most for small business online visibility:

  • AI search readiness
  • Website SEO health
  • Page titles and meta descriptions
  • Content clarity, structure & semantic organisation
  • Internal linking opportunities
  • FAQ suggestions where useful
  • Schema and structured data
  • Local SEO signals
  • Google Business Profile readiness
  • Website visibility monitoring
  • Plain-English progress updates

Built for non-experts

Flavio skips the jargon and tells you what needs attention in plain language, then fixes what it can on its own and guides you through the rest.

Examples of what Flavio can help you understand:

  • Is my homepage clear enough for search engines and AI assistants?
  • Does Google understand what my business does?
  • Is my website prepared for local search?
  • Are there pages that need clearer structure or better content?
  • What has improved since Flavio started working?

Goal-based website improvement

Flavio sets its plan around your goal and works on it automatically, whether that’s:

  • Getting more local customers
  • Improving website visibility in Google
  • Preparing your content for AI-powered search
  • Keeping your website’s SEO healthy over time

AI-powered improvements

Flavio uses AI to prepare, suggest and apply improvements automatically to your site. You can review what changed anytime, and switch to manual approval if you want more control. Flavio can help with:

  • Rewriting page titles
  • Improving headings & meta descriptions
  • Suggesting clearer page copy
  • Creating useful FAQ content
  • Adding structured data
  • Improving local business information
  • Preparing content so search engines and AI assistants can better understand it

You stay in control. Flavio is designed to show recommendations clearly before changes are applied.

Local SEO improvements

Flavio can help identify and improve local SEO signals such as:

  • Business name, address, and phone consistency
  • Local business information
  • Service and location clarity
  • Google Business Profile readiness
  • LocalBusiness schema
  • Pages that should better explain where you work and what you offer

AI search readiness

People increasingly use AI assistants and AI-powered search results to discover businesses, compare options, and make decisions.

Flavio helps prepare your website for this new search behavior by improving:

  • Content clarity
  • Page structure
  • Answer-friendly formatting
  • Schema markup
  • Local business signals
  • Trust and credibility signals
  • Topic relevance

Progress in plain English

Flavio explains progress in language that makes sense. Instead of showing technical scores, Flavio helps you understand:

  • What was found
  • What was improved
  • What still needs attention
  • What Flavio is working on next
  • How your site is becoming clearer, healthier, and more visible

Why use Flavio?

Flavio is a good fit if:

  • You run a small business website on WordPress
  • You want more people to find your business
  • You do not have time to learn SEO
  • You want simple guidance instead of technical dashboards
  • You want your content and structure improved without doing it yourself
  • You care about Google, local visibility, and AI search readiness
  • You want your website to keep improving over time

Free trial and plans

Flavio includes a 30-day Pro trial so you can experience the full Website Growth Agent.

After the trial, access may be limited depending on your plan. You can still review past improvements and upgrade when you want Flavio to keep optimizing your site.

External service disclosure

Flavio connects your WordPress site to the marketgoo platform to scan, analyze, and improve your website, so a marketgoo account is required to activate it. When you activate Flavio, your site may send information such as:

  • Site URL
  • WordPress configuration information
  • Public page content required for analysis
  • SEO metadata
  • Plugin status information
  • Business information entered during setup
  • Scan results and improvement recommendations

This information is used to provide website analysis, SEO recommendations, AI-powered suggestions, visibility monitoring, and related Flavio functionality.

Please review our Privacy Policy and Terms of Service for more information:

Privacy Policy: https://www.marketgoo.com/privacy-policy/
Terms of Service: https://www.marketgoo.com/terms/
Flavio website: https://www.flavioagent.com/
sections.installation:
1. Install Flavio using the WordPress plugin installer, or extract the zip file and drop the contents into the wp-content/plugins/ directory of your WordPress site.
  2. Activate the plugin from the “Plugins” menu in WordPress.
  3. Open Flavio from your WordPress admin menu.
  4. Follow the setup steps to connect your website.
  5. Choose your website goal.
  6. Let Flavio scan your site, create your improvement plan, and get started.
sections.faq:
Is Flavio free?

Flavio includes a 30-day Pro trial. After the trial, some features may require a paid plan. Visit the Flavio website at flavioagent.com for current pricing details.

Does Flavio make changes automatically?

Yes. Flavio is autonomous by default, but you stay in control: depending on your plan, you can adjust how much Flavio does on its own versus what needs your approval before going live.

Do I need SEO knowledge to use Flavio?

No. Flavio is built for non-experts. It explains what matters, recommends what to improve, and helps you take action without needing to understand technical SEO terms.

What does Flavio improve?

Flavio can help improve page titles, meta descriptions, headings, content clarity, FAQs, structured data, local SEO signals, internal links & other elements that help search engines & AI assistants better understand your website.

Does Flavio help with local SEO?

Yes. Flavio can help identify local visibility opportunities, improve local business information, support LocalBusiness schema, improve Google Business Profile readiness, and help your site better communicate what you do & where you’re located.

Does Flavio help my site appear in ChatGPT, Gemini, or other AI assistants?

Flavio structures & clarifies your content so AI systems can read & cite it more easily. No plugin can guarantee inclusion in AI answers, but Flavio improves the foundations that matter for your visibility in AI search

Will Flavio conflict with my existing SEO plugin?

Flavio works with Yoast SEO and All in One SEO. When one of them is active, Flavio saves page titles and meta descriptions in that plugin’s own fields, so your page keeps a single title and description, and your headings and menus stay as they are. It also reads which pages that plugin keeps out of search.

With other SEO plugins, Flavio writes titles and meta descriptions with WordPress itself, and your SEO plugin may show its own instead. Sitemaps and schema from your SEO plugin keep working as they are.

Where can I get support?

You can use the WordPress.org support forum for this plugin or use the support options provided in the plugin.
sections.changelog:
1.14.0

  • [NEW] If your home page is a static page and you don’t use an SEO plugin, Flavio can now change the title shown in search results and browser tabs. Your site name stays at the end of the title (for example, “Fresh bread daily – Rosa’s Bakery”), and your page heading and menus don’t change. Undoing the change brings back WordPress’s default title.
  • [UPDATE] Before you approve a new home page title, the preview now shows it exactly as it will appear, with your site name at the end.
  • [FIX] If your theme or SEO plugin controls a page’s title, Flavio’s changes to it wouldn’t show up. Flavio now leaves those pages alone and explains why in your timeline, instead of making the change anyway and wrongly telling you that you’d changed the title yourself.
  • [FIX] Choosing “Switch to Flavio’s” when there was nothing to change no longer marks the task as done.

1.13.0

  • [NEW] When Flavio rewrites a page, adds an FAQ section or adds your contact details, it now prepares the change as a draft. Preview it on your own site, with your theme, then publish or reject it. Your live page stays untouched until you decide. Works with the WordPress editor, Classic Editor, Elementor (including Elementor 4 widgets), Divi 4 and 5, WPBakery, Avada and Beaver Builder.
  • [NEW] You can also publish or edit the draft from your usual editor. Flavio detects it and records it in your timeline, as if you’d approved it from Flavio.
  • [NEW] After you publish several of Flavio’s drafts for a page builder exactly as prepared, Flavio offers to publish its future changes on that builder without asking. You can undo any of them from your timeline, and if you reject or undo one, Flavio goes back to asking first.
  • [NEW] When you reject a draft, you can say why (it broke your design, doesn’t sound like your business, says something untrue, or the page didn’t need changes).
  • [UPDATE] You can now undo a change straight from the activity timeline: each change that can be reversed has an Undo button next to it.
  • [UPDATE] Flavio now improves more of each page: blurbs, call-to-action boxes, toggles, accordions, tabs, titles and icon lists in the supported page builders, plus GenerateBlocks and Kadence Blocks headings. Rewrites keep your existing links, and each block stays about the same length.
  • [UPDATE] The contact details card now tells you exactly what Flavio is adding (phone number, address or email).
  • [FIX] If a page uses page builder elements Flavio doesn’t support yet, it now says so instead of telling you your content already looks good.
  • [FIX] On Elementor pages, the text that search engines and SEO plugins read is now updated whenever Flavio changes the page.

1.12.0

  • [NEW] Flavio now works with Yoast SEO and All in One SEO. When one is active, the page titles and meta descriptions you approve are saved in that plugin’s own fields, so each page keeps a single title and description, and your headings and menus aren’t affected. Undoing a change restores exactly what the plugin had before.
  • [NEW] If your SEO plugin already shares your business details with search engines, Flavio adds your address and phone number to them instead of creating a second listing, so search engines see one business with complete details.
  • [NEW] If Yoast SEO or All in One SEO hides a page from search, Flavio now tells you and shows the exact steps to fix it in that plugin.
  • [NEW] If a title or description you approved still doesn’t show on the page, Flavio lets you know and asks which version to keep, with tips on where to check.
  • [UPDATE] Before you approve a title or description, Flavio now tells you where it will be saved and what else it affects.
  • [UPDATE] The activity timeline now shows where each title or description was saved (Yoast SEO, All in One SEO or WordPress).
  • [FIX] When Flavio asked which version of a title or description to keep, your choice could be ignored if Flavio had changed that page before. Your choice is now always applied.
  • [FIX] The activity timeline no longer shows “null” when a page had no description before.

1.11.1

  • [UPDATE] The welcome screen after setup is now shorter, so the button to start is visible without scrolling.
  • [FIX] Fixed uneven spacing between paragraphs in the mode cards during setup.
  • [FIX] Sites whose home page shows the latest posts instead of a static page are now recognized, and Flavio no longer flags the home page as missing.

1.11.0

  • [NEW] The “Flavio” entry in your WordPress menu now shows a red bubble with the number of requests waiting for your approval, the same way WordPress does it for Plugins and Comments.
  • [NEW] Flavio now clears your site’s page cache after changes that touch every page (e.g., a new tagline, the “discourage search engines” setting, or your permalink structure) and refreshes the home page before its first analysis. Works with LiteSpeed Cache, WP Rocket, W3 Total Cache, WP Super Cache, WP Fastest Cache and Cache Enabler.
  • [FIX] Fixed an issue where setup could get stuck waiting on an analysis that had already finished, caused by some hosts caching Flavio’s own requests.

1.10.0

  • [NEW] Your monthly report now has a “Your visibility” section. It tells you how many people found you on Google Search and saw your Business Profile listing compared with the month before, and whether ChatGPT and Gemini mention your business when someone asks them for a business like yours in your area. When they do not, it names who they recommend instead, so you know who you are up against. This needs Google connected from your Flavio account; the AI part works on its own for local businesses.
  • [FIX] Before, when you approved a new title for a page, on some sites that title also showed up in the menu: a menu like “Home | Services | Contact” could end up with three very long titles. Now the menu stays as it was and only the page title changes. If you undo the change, the menu is not touched either.
  • [FIX] Before, pages Flavio created for you (location pages, for example) could show up in your menu on their own if you had WordPress’s “Automatically add new top-level pages” option turned on. Now Flavio creates the page and leaves the menu alone: you decide whether to add it.
  • [FIX] Styles from other plugins or themes could break parts of Flavio’s interface, like making the “Mark as decorative” switch appear stuck. Flavio’s styles now take priority, so this can’t happen again.
  • [UPDATE] The “Mark as decorative” switch now shows a check mark and a darker label when it’s on, so its state is clear at a glance.
  • [UPDATE] Dialogs and menus now open and close with a short fade, and closing them no longer flickers.
  • [UPDATE] When Flavio changes a page title or creates a page, the Timeline now tells you what happened to your menu.

1.9.1

  • [UPDATE] The “Safe” agent mode is now called “Essentials”. The name was confusing: it suggested the other two modes were somehow unsafe, when all three let you undo any change at any time. Essentials works exactly as before, applying the routine fixes on its own and asking you before new pages, content rewrites or other important changes. Your current setting stays as it is, nothing to do on your side.

1.9.0

  • [NEW] Flavio now supports sites built with Avada. Your pages keep their styling after Flavio edits them.
  • [FIX] Some screens showed internal code names instead of plain labels, like “focusAreas.homepage.name” instead of “Homepage”. This is now fixed everywhere it appeared.

1.8.0

  • [NEW] Flavio now warns you when it loses access to your Google Business Profile, whether the access was removed from your Google account or disconnected from your Flavio settings. A highlighted notice on the dashboard explains what Flavio can no longer do for you and gives you a single button to reconnect. Once you reconnect, the notice goes away and Flavio picks up the pending Google work on its own.
  • [FIX] Fixed the “You do not have permission to perform this action” error that appeared when you left Flavio open in a browser tab and your WordPress session expired in the meantime. Flavio now renews its access on its own, so in most cases you will not notice anything. When you really do need to log in again, it tells you so and takes you to the WordPress login.
  • [UPDATE] Error screens have a new look: a clear title explaining what happened, a reminder that nothing on your site was changed, and a single button to try again. Technical details stay folded away and only show up when they can help support.

1.7.0

  • [NEW] Flavio now asks for your permission before creating the WordPress Application Password it uses to work on your site. A new step during setup explains what it is (not your login, it cannot sign in to your admin), what Flavio uses it for, and how to revoke it anytime from Users › Profile.
  • [UPDATE] If that credential stops working later on (for example, you revoked it), Flavio no longer recreates it on its own: it pauses and asks for your permission again the next time you open it. Sites already connected keep working as they are.

1.6.0

  • [NEW] A new “Safe” mode, now the recommended way to run Flavio. Flavio applies low-risk fixes on its own (SEO titles and descriptions, image descriptions, duplicate page titles, contact details on your contact page) and asks you before anything bigger: new pages, content rewrites, URL changes, your tagline or your Google Business Profile. Review and Automatic keep working exactly as before, and you can switch between the three modes anytime from Preferences.
  • [NEW] If the address in your business profile and the one on your Google Business Profile don’t match, Flavio now pauses its work on the listing and asks you which one is right. Tell it you fixed the address in Google, or update your Flavio profile with the Google address in one click. Flavio never changes the address on your Google listing, only you can.
  • [NEW] The tagline step during setup can now always be skipped by clicking “I’d rather not change it now”. Skipping leaves your site untouched and setup continues normally.
  • [NEW] When you move Flavio to a more autonomous mode, it offers to take care of any requests still waiting for your approval that the new mode covers. Switching to Safe only picks up the low-risk ones and leaves the rest for you to review.
  • [UPDATE] The “Let me take it from here” suggestion now also shows up in Safe mode, so you can hand the remaining requests to Automatic whenever you are ready.
  • [FIX] Choosing to keep your current tagline no longer rewrites it on your site with the same value. Nothing is changed unless you pick a new one.

1.5.1

  • [FIX] Fixed an error on the Activity screen (“Our servers are having issues”) and in the dashboard’s recent improvements widget on sites where another plugin conflicted with how Flavio requested the timeline.

1.5.0

  • [NEW] When your hosting blocks outside access to your site (for example an anti-bot protection), Flavio now shows a dedicated screen explaining what is happening and how to fix it, including a ready-to-send message for your hosting provider.
  • [UPDATE] While your site stays unreachable, Flavio pauses its work instead of trying blindly, and resumes automatically within a few hours once access is restored, with no need to reconnect.
  • [FIX] Fixed a bug where the connection check reported success even when an anti-bot tool was actually blocking Flavio.

1.4.0

  • [NEW] If your site can’t connect (missing HTTPS, a security plugin blocking access, or a hosting configuration issue), Flavio now shows you exactly what’s wrong and how to fix it, including a ready-to-send message for your hosting provider
  • [NEW] Flavio verifies its connection right after setup, so hosting issues are caught on the spot instead of failing silently later
  • [UPDATE] If the connection breaks later on, Flavio repairs it automatically the next time you open it and picks up right where it left off
  • [FIX] Reconnecting is now safer: a failed attempt never invalidates credentials that were still working
  • [FIX] Uninstalling the plugin now removes all of Flavio’s access credentials from your site

1.3.0

  • [NEW] Flavio can now update content on pages built with the Classic Editor
  • [UPDATE] The activity timeline now shows when Flavio started working on each part of your site, and the exact date of every change made
  • [UPDATE] Added an extra check (‘sanitization’) on AI-generated content before it’s published to your site
  • [UPDATE] Activity and requests for your product pages are now grouped by page, with a filter to see only what’s waiting for your approval
  • [FIX] The requests list no longer gets stuck loading in some situations
  • [FIX] Fixed an issue that could make Flavio process the same task over and over

1.2.0

  • [NEW] Switch to Automatic mode right from your requests list, and clear everything Flavio can handle in one go
  • [NEW] A confirmation screen every time you switch between Automatic and Manual Review, so you always know what’s changing
  • [UPDATE] Requests are now grouped by Area, with the newest ones first
  • [UPDATE] Clearer button copy, so it’s obvious whether you’re publishing a change or leaving things as they are

1.1.0

  • [NEW] Automated on-page optimization: titles, meta descriptions, image alt text, FAQs, and structured data
  • [NEW] Page builder compatibility with Elementor, Divi, Gutenberg, Classic Editor, Beaver Builder
  • [NEW] Business profile setup with Google Places address autocomplete
  • [NEW] Guided Google Business Profile connection and description improvements
  • [NEW] Local SEO improvements: NAP consistency checks, contact page creation, and location pages
  • [NEW] Content strategy tools: duplicate title detection and content improvement suggestions
  • [NEW] Monthly site status reports with progress tracking
  • [NEW] Activity timeline showing every change Flavio makes to your site
  • [NEW] One-click undo for reversible changes
  • [NEW] Friendly, more readable URL suggestions
  • [UPDATE] Expanded error detection for broken pages and indexing issues

1.0.0

  • Initial release
  • AI-powered SEO suggestions
  • XML sitemap generator
  • Robots.txt manager
  • Broken links detection and automatic fixing
  • SEO site scan functionality
  • Task management system
  • Progress tracking and reporting
  • REST API integration
  • Modern admin interface
